questions.question: RNA produced from a fragment of DNA has the sequence of UAAGGC. The sequence of the non-template strand in the DNA that gave rise to this sequence is which one of the following?
questions.explanation:
The non-template strand or coding strand in the DNA will have the same sequence of the RNA
that is produced, except that the non-template or coding strand has T is in place of U.
As all sequences are written in the 5’ to 3’ direction, unless otherwise specified, an RNA sequence
of UAAGGC would correspond to a DNA sequence, on the non-template strand, of TAAGGC. Both
the non-template strand and RNA produced will be a complementary sequence to the template
strand. Therefore, the template strand would be ATTCCG (written 5’ to 3’).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about mRNA splicing is true?

options.text: The existence of split genes has no advantage
Self-splicing introns do not require the help of any protein for splicing to occur accurately
β-thalassaemia results from a genetic defect in the spliceosome

questions.explanation:
Self-splicing introns do not require a spliceosome or any other proteins for the splicing reaction.
Self-splicing introns fold into complex loops and undergo transesterification reactions, thus
undergoing self splicing.
Other options:
Option A: Split genes have the advantage that they allow alternative splicing so that a single gene
can code for variant forms of the same protein.
Option C: B-thalassemia results from the faulty splicing of the B-globin transcript. However, the
spliceosome is normal and the reason for the fault is a mutation in the B-globin gene itself.
Option D: Splicing occurs in the nucleus and mature transcripts are then transported into the
cytosol for translation (protein synthesis) to occur.
